characterList.description: A woman with long dark curly hair, wearing a blue and white patterned tunic-style top with a long necklace and black pants. She is presenting the talk and has tattoos on her left arm.
characterList.name: Kaye Maree Dunn

content_metadata.description: A detailed analysis of a presentation by Kaye Maree Dunn discussing the journey to develop a digital platform for indigenous knowledge management and the initial idea of an indigenous cryptocurrency, Indigicoin.

qAndA.question: What is the Maori word for 'genealogy'?
What is the name of the indigenous cryptocurrency the speaker initially wanted to create?

qAndA.answer: A car journey from Waiuku back to Auckland City.
qAndA.question: What type of journey did the speaker describe that helped her to formulate the idea of creating an indigenous cryptocurrency?
What is the name of the digital platform for storing and managing indigenous knowledge?

qAndA.answer: It likely represents the concept of interconnectedness and decentralized knowledge sharing central to blockchain and indigenous practices.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the woven mat pattern shown in the video?

youtube_description:
EHF Fellow Kaye Maree Dunn is the co-founder of Āhau, a new digital identity platform to help indigenous people connect with their roots. 

This video was filmed at New Frontiers / Te Tūhura Nuku - November 2018 in Upper Hutt, New Zealand. https://www.newfrontiers.nz

New Frontiers is hosted by the Edmund Hillary Fellowship (EHF), a global community of changemakers based out of Aotearoa New Zealand. EHF brings together humankind’s creative potential and entrepreneurial spirit in New Zealand, to build and support innovative ventures for global impact, in partnership with New Zealand's Global Impact Visa. Apply today for the opportunity of a lifetime! - https://www.ehf.org

Subscribe to the EHF channel to watch more videos from this event and from our inspiring community: https://youtube.com/user/kiwiconnectedu?sub_confirmation=1

Heartfelt thanks to Te Ati Awa, the local Māori iwi in the Wellington region who are mana whenua over these lands, and an EHF partner: https://teatiawa.iwi.nz/
